elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a) says "Such audit shall occur no more than once per Calendar Year". Calendar Year is a fixed January-December window (Def. 1.11), so audits in December and the following January would both be permitted; this is not a cap on any rolling 12-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a) sets "at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice", short of 30 days (and the notice is not expressly required to be written).
No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in rendered 9.9(a), (c) or (d); the drafter expressly declined to press it.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) retained: "permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, to audit the books and records".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: 9.9(d) retained: "the Parties shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site or location language in the rendered clause; audit location is unaddressed.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c) fixes the cost-shift trigger at "more than ten percent (10%)", not 5 percent.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: No express prohibition on access to Customer systems was inserted; the clause only scopes the audit to "the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8", which is an implicit limit, not the operative no-systems-access term the element requires.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall occur no more than once per Calendar Year", with the open-ended "unless for cause" escape deleted, so the annual cap is effective.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "but in any event at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice", replacing the [***] blank.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c): "The auditing Party shall bear the full cost of such audit unless such audit reveals an underpayment ... more than ten percent (10%) of the amount set forth in such report"; as applied to an audit of us, the auditing Vendor bears cost below that threshold.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the frequency cap, the 15-day notice floor and the 10 percent cost-shift trigger are each stated in operative language rather than left as [***] blanks or promised in the comment.
Deleting "unless for cause" is necessary rather than extra: an open-ended for-cause exception would defeat the once-per-year cap, so the deletion is inside the frequency element.

Preferred level fails on notice (15 vs 30 days), cost trigger (10 vs 5 percent), and the absent business-hours, off-site and no-systems-access terms; preferred frequency also fails literally because a fixed Calendar Year cap permits two audits within a rolling 12-month span. To reach preferred the drafter would need: "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice"; "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"; "during normal business hours"; "remotely or off-site where reasonably possible, with no direct access to the audited Party's systems"; and a five percent (5%) cost-shift trigger.

Minimality holds: the retained [***] look-back period, the waiver sentence, the independent-auditor and auditor-confidentiality language and the reciprocal structure are untouched, and no survival tail, expense or procedural extras were added.

Intent preserved: the cross-reference to "such [***] period" still resolves to the retained look-back blank, Section 9.8 records scope is unchanged, and no retained sentence contradicts the new limits. The limits bind both Parties, which mildly constrains our own audit right but does not defeat the rule's protective purpose.
